title: Progressing nicely visually. My turn based strategy game
author: Tom_Baron
selftext:
This will be a 48 vs 48 multiplayer turn based strategy game. I am an analyst by trade and am recognised for finding creative solutions to problems in my professional capacity, so creating and tuning gameplay is absolute bread and butter and heaven for me! However, I dont often need 3d models in a finance dashboard. 

This is major iteration 6 or 7 of the city scape and action replays. 100s of minor tweaks and tunes occurred within that and I am  finally starting to feel what I wanted to see in my mind is in front of my eyes. There are a number of further tweaks Ill make to AOE stuff like the thermobaric warhead doesnt create its distinctive cloud of fire but I think the general visual feel is about there. 

The general premise of the game is you are on one side of a two side battle with up to 47 other people, you fight a tactical battle in the midst of a strategic war, how you spend your resources and help your allies is critical to the sides survival. You are primarily rewarded for your side winning, greed really hurts your chances of winning,  If your city is on its last legs, you can even disregard your remaining air defences to launch a huge attack on your opponent.

Even if your city is eliminated, you can assist in the intelligence layer. by analysing the opposition, finding weaknesses and directing your team to them, or spotting an ally in trouble and coordinating reinforcements with your side.

I'm basically building the optimal form of the game I want to play!

comments.author: West_Satisfaction299
comments.body: That's what I did with my game. This looks gorgeous. How are you going to handle the network code for 48 v 48?

replies.author: Tom_Baron
replies.body:
Ah thanks! Its almost all typescript/Webgl and already spun up for testing. Being turn based (you are seeing an action replay in the vid) shouuuullllddd help with egress being the server only really needs to send packets at initialisation of the game for graphics/UI, then intermittently for chat, notifications, heartbeat and deltas at end of turn. I wouldn't have dared try build a RTS with a 96 player cap :D

Persistent storage will be added so I can add the trading blows equivalent of correspondence chess. 1 day per phase for those that dont have an hour or two spare for a game.

comments.author: MechaLenin111
comments.body: This looks really good. This the opposite of AI slop. How do you make explosions?

replies.author: Tom_Baron
replies.body:
They are the product entirely of iteration :). the original explosions were 2d vectors on an isometric vector drawn city, I spent a fair amount of time iterating over the size, colour and variations for different warheads, ensuring they all were working in that design. Then when I flipped over to using three.js webgl 3d visuals. Opus took them into blender and modelled them to fit the rest of the design, taking with it all the specifications of the previous iteration. So nothing magic, technical and I'm in no way skilled artistically. I just had in my head how things should look and knew roughly the path to get me near.  You can see from my previous posts the various iterations :)

This is likely not as far as the graphics go either. There are still a few details Id like to clear up.

comments.author: Wooden_Plant7504
comments.body: This looks really good! I'd play that. Could you share more info about your setup ? Which AI/subscription do you use ? How much time did it take you to reach this stage ? How long do you think until it is "finished" ?

replies.author: Tom_Baron
replies.body:
Thanks! Glad you like the look of it! Its been about a month from conception to the current version. 4 hours a day almost every day and thinking about it a good 20 hours a day 😆. Ive got codex, claude and meshy. I dont do anything special other than really engage with my prompts and the process. I use AI in my professional capacity as a system analyst and have used it for four years now which probably helps, as does the job role.

TLDR with example of how I work and how long this may take, I put a new UI in last night, its a sketch of a UI on this first iteration, fundamentally, the panes are laid out the right way now, the dynamism in the layout works when the game phase switches and that is fundamentally how I want things to work. Like a sketch is fundamentally like a picture you want to paint should look. But none of the detail is there yet. Is it seamless when selecting your defensive units? Are the reports telling you what you need to know? Ill spend hours testing and noting down things I want to "paint the detail into" and likely iterate for days over it. Then ill do exactly the same thing with the visual side of the UI. Ill then hit a point in which its closer to my vision than it was. Ill then work on the next weakest link in the chain and return to the UI later to bring it even closer.

replies.author: Wooden_Plant7504
replies.body: 1 month ? seems you are moving fast. Thanks for replying. Looking forward to trying it when it comes out.
